claims.claim: Remote finding discovery uses deterministic task_run_prefix to narrow git ref search and verifies task identity and revision before structural commit tree inspection, ensuring unrelated historical remediation branches sharing a finding id (e.g. RUN-041-002-F1) are ignored and do not trigger discovery failures for the current task.

Remediation lineages from another revision of the same task are excluded from candidacy during remote finding discovery and direct candidate resolution, preserving exact task and revision binding without raising false fatal errors.

Malformed or incomplete remediation lineages matching the exact requested task revision fail closed with ReviewTransportError or resolution errors before RUN admission, ensuring no Executor invocation occurs.
Ambiguous candidate lineages sharing the exact requested task revision and finding id fail closed with an explicit ambiguity error without applying any heuristic ordering or selection.

Standard successful remediation workflow via --finding preserves single RUN admission, single Executor invocation, exact reviewed-SHA validation, affected verification, and correction lineage semantics.
Explicit artifact remediation mode and REPAIR workflows retain their existing behavior, with no changes to schemas, publication authority, or historical repository refs.

Implementation is strictly bounded to deterministic identity resolution hardening in review transport and operator remediation resolution without retries, fallbacks, model reasoning, or branch mutations.
